title: Originally a webdev but always wanted to get into game design, but never found the time. Now Claude has allowed me to get my first experience and I really enjoyed it.
author: IntelligentLeading11
selftext:
Hey! After spending a month in Germany, 5 minutes away from the legendary Nurburgring, I became inspired to make this retro arcade game based on the Tourist event held in the 20 kilometers long Nordschleife track. For those of you who never heard of the Norsdchleife, it's a legendary race track known as the most dangerous in the world and anyone can enter it with their own car and drive around it at their own pace (there's no speed limit so some folks drive it with very fast cars at the limit) for around 30 euros. That may seem cheap but if you crash (and MANY do), the costs can become astronomical very fast.

I spent a while at the Nordschleife, going in the track with my own car and some rentals, also attending many car events and races. I also traveled a lot around the area which has amazing mountain roads with a lot of supercars driving around. You can say this game has a lot of little details that come straight from my own experience living in the area. As an extra benefit, if you ever plan on going to the Nordschleife, you can learn all the corners/corner names by playing this game!

I'm a professional web developer so naturally I made this as a browser game, so you can play it basically on anything that runs a browser. The idea is to evoke the feelings of the games in the past, where you failed and failed until you passed the level and got great satisfaction from it. I have a lot of cool ideas to add more modes to the game but first I need to learn if anyone likes the game to begin with 😄 . So I appreciate any feedback if you get to try it (except asking for better graphics, we already have Assetto Corsa for realism/simulation). Also if you find the slower cars too easy make sure to reach the faster car on green hell mode and see how you do with that one 😉

Regarding AI development, I used Claude Fable/opus as I do normally at my job. Absolutely all of the game design/mechanics come from me, the agent helped with the assets/sfx/menus. There's not much else worth mentioning I believe, these new models are just too good. Even detractors are starting to admit this tech is wild beyond our dreams. Development/deployment took a couple of days 🤯 . The idea itself you could say took a lifetime of experiences driving/tracking cars, being finalized by me being able to finally visit the Nurburgring for the first time after decades of dreaming about it.

PS: I can't link the game's url because for some strange reason Reddit doesn't like that domain, so you'll have to get it from the video at the very end.

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: Glad to see people jumping into their dream of making games. The current graphics remind me of my Atari Lynx. Bright colors and chunky pixels. The driving feel is good, uhm, except for that turn. I guess I DID rush my first lap. I made my own [racing game](https://vibecodedgames.itch.io/pavement) but went with a 2D view.

replies.author: IntelligentLeading11
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/adansekf5yrh1.png?width=1670&format=png&auto=webp&s=f074bee8d429e678e0bf74764b35696953ec4ac2

Nice one! It reminds me of my game in some areas except with an aerial view. Very cool. I beat two stages and left it open to keep playing later. Great effort with this one, I'm being 100% honest, not just being nice because you commented on my post. Just curious, what was the response to your game so far?

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: If we remove all "oh no it's A.I." responses, every one tends to like it, though some feel it's not very original, but some unique features are that it has procedural roads and weather that are different every season you race. There is a "road trip" mode that is just a relaxing view. Plus you can play as the cops. It's essentially the biggest and most complex game I've designed and am learning a lot from doing it. Few people seem to notice it's one program that runs on desktop or mobile browser. Classic "Web designer tries to vibe code a game" :) I made a responsive game.

replies.author: IntelligentLeading11
replies.body: Sweet! I need to look into that procedural generation thingy. By the way, I tried the game on my Macbook and it ran great 👌
